members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py eagerly runs json.loads on any string parameter whose annotation is a union containing str (most commonly `str | None`), so a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-serialized payload passed as a string arg, or literal "123"/"true") gets silently corrupted into a parsed dict/list/int/bool before Pydantic validation. Both PRs touch the exact same guard clause in pre_parse_json and add a new predicate helper to decide when to skip the json.loads call. (2 PRs)

members.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs replace the same `field_info.annotation is not str` check in pre_parse_json with a smarter predicate, but they differ in exactly which annotations are covered. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json calls get_origin/get_args directly on the union members and skips parsing whenever every member is in a fixed {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} set — it does not unwrap Annotated, so it misses the very common MCP pattern where a parameter is written as `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (Annotated-wrapped str combined with None). #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated step before checking the union members, so it correctly detects and skips pre-parsing for that Annotated-wrapped optional-str case in addition to the plain `str | None` case. #2032 is broader in one respect (it also skips parsing for str|int/str|bool unions), but that widens the behavior change beyond the reported bug and isn't exercised by either PR's own tests based on the diffs shown; #3056's narrower, explicitly-named fix (_is_optional_str) plus Annotated-unwrapping handles the real-world case the bug report is about without the extra surface area.

members.title: fix: don't send a response for cancelled requests
members.author: Zelys-DFKH

Applying both would conflict on the same lines in `cancel()` since #2493's deletion and #2514's replacement-with-notification touch the identical region.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs replace the same `field_info.annotation is not str` check in pre_parse_json with a smarter predicate, but they differ in exactly which annotations are covered. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json calls get_origin/get_args directly on the union members and skips parsing whenever every member is in a fixed {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} set — it does not unwrap Annotated, so it misses the very common MCP pattern where a parameter is written as `Annotated[str, Field(description=...)] | None` (Annotated-wrapped str combined with None). #3056 adds an explicit _unwrap_annotated step before checking the union members, so it correctly detects and skips pre-parsing for that Annotated-wrapped optional-str case in addition to the plain `str | None` case. #2032 is broader in one respect (it also skips parsing for str|int/str|bool unions), but that widens the behavior change beyond the reported bug and isn't exercised by either PR's own tests based on the diffs shown; #3056's narrower, explicitly-named fix (_is_optional_str) plus Annotated-unwrapping handles the real-world case the bug report is about without the extra surface area.

members.title: fix: skip JSON pre-parsing for str union annotations in pre_parse_json
members.author: adityuhkapoor
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3056: pre_parse_json in func_metadata.py eagerly runs json.loads on any string parameter whose annotation is a union containing str (most commonly `str | None`), so a plain string value that happens to look like JSON (e.g. a JSON-serialized payload passed as a string arg, or literal "123"/"true") gets silently corrupted into a parsed dict/list/int/bool before Pydantic validation. Both PRs touch the exact same guard clause in pre_parse_json and add a new predicate helper to decide when to skip the json.loads call.
